claim_boundary: Research documentation only. No claim for or against the Riemann Hypothesis.

nodes.name: Positive-cone blindness
nodes.definition: A certificate whose premises retain only the positive measure, negative support, window degree, and nonnegative source terms is invariant under scaling the negative mass, so it cannot certify a signed moment inequality; a metric comparison is necessary.

edges.note: Coefficient-square positivity does not compare the prime-channel mass with the positive channel.
Positive lattice counts and the pure Eisenstein pairing are invariant under negative-mass scaling.
The positive diagonal GNS metric does not control the signed Weil defect.
Positive edge-value seeds retain no metric ratio between the two moment measures.
The SOS language exists exactly for an empty negative register; the surviving comparison restates positivity.
Value-preserving orientation is available exactly in the positive-measure class.
Canonical Hamiltonian positivity is the existing signed-moment pivot condition, not an independent source.
The exact product law synchronizes signs and contributes no second positivity condition.
One surviving target is a representation-theoretic proof of the metric moment-cone comparison nu <= mu.
The alternative surviving template is operator positivity with a proved explicit-formula bridge.
